question: Psychiatric consultation is mandatory for all patients admitted with deliberate self-poisoning (DSP), and should be arranged before discharge regardless of whether the patient denies suicidal intent at the time of clinical interview.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This is TRUE. Patients who deny suicidal intent after DSP are NOT cleared for discharge without psychiatric review. The index episode is the greatest predictor of repeat attempt and completed suicide. Psychiatric consultation before discharge is a mandatory, non-negotiable clinical and medico-legal standard.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Psychiatric referral after deliberate self-poisoning is mandatory — denial of suicidal intent at interview does not eliminate the risk. The index DSP episode is the strongest predictor of future completed suicide. Assessment must include mental state examination, risk stratification, and a safety plan. The patient should NOT be discharged without psychiatric clearance.
